open_points.subject: A18 retention clock and backup-record instant
open_points.text: The clock is read to the microsecond, and a backup's record holds its instant in UTC to the microsecond (L16), so the cutoff and every record's instant have one precision and are compared as they are, neither rounded nor truncated;
open_points.question: What exact representation supplies a microsecond clock reading and stores the record instant, and what happens when the underlying wall clock has finer precision: must the time source already return an exact microsecond value, or is the value rounded or truncated before use?
options: The clock contract returns a UTC-aware instant already quantized to microseconds, so no conversion occurs.
Truncate a finer clock reading to microseconds.
Round a finer clock reading to the nearest microsecond.
Store and compare an integer count of microseconds from a declared epoch.
Store a UTC textual timestamp with exactly six fractional digits and define its conversion rule.
open_points.default_guess: Require the clock contract to return a UTC-aware instant already quantized to microseconds and serialize it with exactly six fractional digits, rejecting values with another precision.

witness.initial: A kept backup records 2026-10-12T03:00:00.000000Z, and the physical UTC wall-clock instant at the start of retention step 3 is 2026-11-11T03:00:00.0000006Z.
events: Registry starts step 3 and obtains the wall-clock reading.
One implementation truncates the finer reading to 2026-11-11T03:00:00.000000Z; another rounds it to 2026-11-11T03:00:00.000001Z.
Each subtracts 720 hours and compares the recorded backup instant with its cutoff.
outcomes: The truncated cutoff equals the backup instant, so the backup is kept.
The rounded cutoff is one microsecond later than the backup instant, so the backup is deleted.
witness.observer: The owner inspecting the kept backups or the newest-backup display.

open_points.subject: A18 Required tests item 7
open_points.text:
With the step's cutoff fixed at its start, a kept backup made exactly
   30 × 24 hours before it is kept and one made a microsecond earlier is
   deleted; a record instant with a non-zero fraction of a second is
   compared with that fraction, not at the whole second.
open_points.question: Relative to which instant must the two backup-record instants be constructed: the retention step's cutoff instant, the instant at which each backup was originally renamed to its kept name, or another instant?
options: The first record instant equals the retention cutoff and the second is cutoff minus one microsecond.
The intervals are measured backward from the time each backup was originally made kept.
The intervals are measured backward from the start of the test's retention step.
open_points.default_guess: Rewrite the test to say that the first record instant equals the step's cutoff and the second equals the cutoff minus one microsecond.

open_points.subject: A18 retention precision
open_points.text: The clock is read to the microsecond, and a backup's record holds its instant in UTC to the microsecond (L16), so the cutoff and every record's instant have one precision and are compared as they are, neither rounded nor truncated; a backup whose instant is earlier than the cutoff is deleted.
open_points.rule: У значения, которое читает генерируемый код, ровно три пути; путь выбирается по тому, что это за значение, и у значения один дом (§15.4).
open_points.question: The passage must place the microsecond precision and representation on one declared path to generated code—through the applicable model type, an imported data-provider constant, or the time-source backend—and name that path instead of leaving the value only in prose.
